newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Protestors stall Guatemala crude exports, pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Protestors stall Guatemala crude exports, pipeline.

text.p: Hundreds of protestors, including crude oil truck drivers, have stalled oil exports and work on an almost-completed pipeline in northern Guatemala, the president of Basic Petroleum International Ltd said Tuesday.

Basic president Rodolfo Sosa told Reuters that Guatemala's only oil producer is still trucking crude to the coast, but the protest and a truckers strike have slowed down daily transport. He declined to say to what extent exports have been limited.
Basic produces 20,000 barrels of crude a day, most of which are exported.
Hundreds of protestors have been demonstrating since Monday and are asking the government to permanently stop the pipeline.
The uprising comes two weeks after about 50 of 300 oil truck drivers for Basic went on strike, apparently fearing their jobs would disappear soon after the completion of the pipeline.

The new pipeline, Basic's third, will run from La Libertad to Raxruja in remote, northern Guatemala and allow the company to move oil from the remote Xan oil fields to ports on the Caribbean coast without using trucks.
